- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high.
- If sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model overfits short-term volatility; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is positive and recent price is trending down — adjust upward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >10% below), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean — apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment is uniformly negative and price is trending down, model tends to forecast a false recovery — suppress upward bias in next 7 days.
